omissions.description: The candidates do not operationalize the source's specific research methods and the distinct hypothesis inputs each method supplies, beyond the general instruction to produce an evidence-backed hypothesis.
omissions.quote:
Analytics funnel analysis (GA4, Shopify): find the step with the biggest drop and the most traffic. Feeds where to test.

Session replay: watch real sessions to see rage clicks, dead clicks, loops, form abandonment. Feeds what is confusing.

Heatmaps/scroll maps: see what gets attention and what is missed. Feeds hypotheses about placement and reach. Weight by revenue per click, not raw clicks.

On-site surveys (exit intent, post-purchase): ask why people did not buy or almost did not. Feeds objections.

User testing: watch 5-8 people attempt a task and narrate. Feeds usability problems.

Customer interviews: understand motivation, anxiety, and the words customers use. Feeds messaging hypotheses.

omissions.description: No supported action directs the required test-duration rule, including reaching the pre-computed sample size and avoiding an early stop based only on significance.
omissions.quote: Test duration: at least one full week, in practice two, plus enough to hit the pre-computed sample size. Do not stop just because you hit significance early.

omissions.description: No supported action directs the source's specific mitigation for the high variance of revenue-based metrics.
omissions.quote: Mitigate by winsorizing outlier orders or using a threshold proportion metric (share of visitors who spend more than $X) so no single large order dominates.

source_limitations: This is a bounded excerpt labeled “batch”; adjacent source context, definitions, and any qualifications outside the excerpt are unavailable.
Several platform, legal, vendor, and historical assertions are attributed to named external sources or organizations, but the underlying primary materials are not included for verification here.

The excerpt does not define several operational terms or thresholds it relies on, including “a few thousand” orders per month, MDE, a “point of evidence,” a winsorizing threshold, and the threshold value $X.

The numerical traffic and variance figures are presented for a stated illustrative ecommerce case and baseline; the excerpt does not establish that they generalize to other traffic, conversion, or order-value distributions.
